An admin account's Leave, and its Decline of an invitation that made it an admin, return AdminCannotSelfRemove before anything is written or sent: when requires_self_demote_before_leave is true, call self_demote_admin first and then Leave or Decline; a last admin first makes another member an admin. With experimental device groups on, User Leave instead demotes a nonlast active admin account itself before SelfRemove, can_leave includes that Leave and requires_self_demote_before_leave is false; the last active admin account is refused on all its devices before any new choice or departure publication. The coarse chat-list Leave action opens the authoritative command and need not imply last-admin eligibility. Sign-out records no Decline; in a chat the account administers with another account it steps the account down first (mdk#2818). A recorded Decline remains if a later eligibility check refuses departure; a committed demotion remains if the following Leave fails. Already admitted native work retains its ordinary retry owner. A SelfRemove applied without readable sibling attribution establishes no new automatic-Add hold, and later repair does not promise to recover that attribution retroactively.

A leave can become blocked after it was accepted: if the selected branch makes the account the group's last active admin (two admins left at once and the other's step-down won, say), no Commit can finish the leave. The chat keeps reading as leaving (leave_request_pending), and leave_blocked is set on the group record, the chat-list row and management state. MDK does not retry, rejoin or reverse a Decline on its own. Show "Can't leave: you're the only admin" with a Cancel action while can_cancel_leave holds; cancel_leave clears the leave on this device and the chat reads as joined again. To leave after that, make another member an admin, demote, and Leave again.

A local chat copy that has applied its own removal stays terminal: later branch changes do not resume convergence on that copy. Rejoining requires a fresh valid Welcome that replaces its cryptographic state; an invitation alone is not a guarantee of recovery. The remaining members do not promise to recommit every removal forever. An admin's account-removal intent has at most two reissues, targeting members still in the selected membership. The rebuilt commit must pass the author's current admin-authority check when it is sent; otherwise the queued send is refused and retired. Device-removal cleanup has its own current-roster and remembered-key conditions. An eligible chat admin can remove a stale member account with remove_members, which removes every leaf of that account, including its active devices; it is not a per-device cleanup control. Removing a linked device is a separate device-group action. Automatic inactivity removal is not available yet. Keep showing the selected membership and removal outcome rather than assuming every branch has permanently removed a leaf.

At the maximum decision version, an opposite invitation choice is refused and the held winner remains; ordinary User Leave still proceeds without writing another version. Retained invitation generations have no expiry or count cap: a malicious currently linked device can inflate stored decisions and broadcast pages.

linked_devices(account_ref) returns this account's own devices as LinkedDeviceFfi records, read from the roster of the device group this device trusts, for a Devices screen:

  • This device comes first (is_this_device), then the rest by linked_at. Every entry is this account's own device.
  • slot_id_hex is the device's KeyPackage slot, the handle later device actions take. label, client and platform are empty until set; linked_by_slot_id_hex is None for the device that founded the group.
  • Each device writes its own client and platform: its clientName and devicePlatform options (a short name such as iOS), trimmed, and empty when blank or over 64 bytes. It writes them with its next KeyPackage announcement in the device group, so they appear after its next maintenance pass.
  • last_active_at is when a heartbeat last showed a sibling running, in Unix seconds. Each running device sends one in the device group at most once an hour; each is dated when it was created or, if earlier, when this device read it. It is None for this device and for a sibling none of whose heartbeats has counted yet.
  • inactive is this device's own judgement, for showing the user: 30 days have passed since a sibling's last activity or since this device first found it in the roster, whichever is later. It is never set for this device. status Inactive is the roster's own mark.
  • The account's devices mark and remove inactive devices themselves. A device counts time only while it is caught up with its device group, and restarts every count after more than 24 hours without being caught up. About 30 days after a sibling was last heard from, a caught-up device marks it Inactive: show "Remove" and "Keep" for a device whose status is Inactive and whose keep_while_inactive is off. About 90 days after, a device still marked Inactive without Keep while inactive is removed as by remove_linked_device, except that its KeyPackage slot is left on the relays. A marked device that is running clears its own mark once it has caught up. One whose recovery gave up on a missed Commit, or whose copy is unrecoverable with no automatic rejoin underway, can't catch up, see or clear its mark, and is removed at 90 days like one that never came back: offer the reset on device_group_stalled (below).
  • The list is empty until this device trusts a device group (a single-device account has none), and in ordinary opens without explicit experimental device-group intent.
  • The device group's own events never reach hosts. Re-read on MarmotEventFfi::LinkedDevicesChanged, which carries no device or group identities. With device groups on, it also fires once each time the account's worker opens or reconnects, so it may fire with no visible change.

Chat history from another device: each imported TimelineMessageRecordFfi names its source in imported_from, and chat_history_imports(account_ref) lists each held chat's history as Receiving (retrying once an attempt to get its bundle failed) or Imported. The list is empty and the event silent in ordinary opens without explicit experimental device-group intent. Draw "Imported from <device>" where rows change from imported to live, and say "another device" for an empty device_label. Re-read the list on MarmotEventFfi::ChatHistoryImportsChanged, which fires whenever its answer changes, a source device's rename or removal included; re-read rows on LinkedDevicesChanged for their new names.

rename_linked_device(account_ref, slot_id_hex, label) renames any of the account's devices, this one included, with one roster commit in the device group:

  • Only the label changes. It is at most 64 bytes of UTF-8; an empty label clears it.
  • It is refused with nothing sent (MarmotKitError.Runtime with details device group refused: <reason>) in ordinary opens, for a label that is too long, without a device group, for a slot the roster doesn't list, and while the device group has an earlier change of this device's in flight (device_group_busy). Retry that last one later; a commit then could build on a roster that is about to change.
  • A rename whose commit loses a fork is made again on a later maintenance pass, unless another rename or settings edit of that device won; that one stands. Show the label linked_devices returns after LinkedDevicesChanged, not the one the user typed.

update_linked_device_settings(account_ref, slot_id_hex, add_to_all_chats, bring_history, keep_while_inactive) changes any linked device's supplied settings, this device included. Each setting is optional: omitted values come from the current roster on the account worker, so changing one toggle does not restore another from a stale screen. A patch that still matches after earlier-edit recovery sends no new edit. Enabling Add to all my chats permits eligible direct post-link Adds while that flow is still adding, and gap filling under its conditions; turning it off does not leave joined chats. The approving device's direct post-link pass sends no gap-fill claim (kind 458). With three or more devices, it can race another sibling's gap filling and cause extra Add attempts, private-KeyPackage consumption, or Commits and convergence passes; selected-parent presence checks and ordinary branch selection still apply. Bring chat history applies to future sibling Adds and transfers still owed; enabling it does not backfill chats already joined or recreate a transfer discarded while it was off. Keep while inactive stops automatic removal of an Inactive device; it does not stop the mark, explicit removal or sign-out.

Automatic chat Adds can wait for compatible private KeyPackages. Held packages that satisfy stock time checks but lack a capability a waiting chat requires do not cover that chat's need: while the issuing device's leaf in the device group advertises what the chat requires, this device asks it for more, and the compatible packages it hands over complete the Add. The older packages stay for chats they fit. A device whose leaf does not advertise the requirement is not asked on that chat's behalf; its own upkeep still stops counting packages that no longer advertise its current capabilities and hands over compatible replacements. An issuer holding as many issued packages as it keeps answers with packages it already handed over, so the chat can wait for older stock to expire. Repeat requests for an unchanged unmet need keep their hourly throttle; an increased need can make a request due at the next upkeep. Progress depends on the issuer and device group being available, with no fast or guaranteed discovery deadline for this wait.

On the editing device, new automatic Adds and history transfers wait for a differing local setting intention to settle. Existing history debt keeps its original expiry; once ready, a history setting that is off discards that debt. This does not recall deliveries already handed off or change what another device sends before it learns the edit.

A linked device added to a chat with a private KeyPackage that expired before it opened the Welcome can never join that copy. Once that device has been heard from for an hour after the expiry, a sibling removes its unused leaf and gap filling adds it again, so the chat shows a removal and an Add of the same account's device. Bring chat history applies to that Add as to any other. A device that joined but never updated its leaf in the chat is treated the same way. A device not heard from since the expiry keeps its leaf, and a restart of the sibling that would remove it starts that hour again.

A rename and a settings change share one recovery record. Before accepting another edit of that device, the runtime tries the existing recovery of an earlier lost edit and re-reads the roster. Retry device_group_busy only while it remains unsettled. A successful no-op never leaves an opposite lost intention to apply later. A competing user edit of that device wins as a whole, even if it changed a different toggle. Once an edit is retired because another edit stands or the device leaves the roster, a later branch that removes that rival does not restore the retired local choice. To apply it again, edit the device once it is listed in the selected roster. Refresh the displayed label and flags on LinkedDevicesChanged. These commands remain behind the device-group development gate.

Explicit local device-group reset before fresh pairing

DeviceLinkSnapshotFfi.device_group_stalled says this device can no longer catch up with its device group: automatic recovery gave up on a change it missed, or its copy is unrecoverable and automatic rejoin is not underway. It cannot see or clear an Inactive mark, and its siblings remove it about 90 days after they last heard from it. Offer the reset below, then fresh pairing. Re-read on DeviceLinkChanged, which fires when it changes.

In an experimental device-group build, offer reset_device_group_for_repair(account_ref) only after the user chooses to discard this device's local hidden device-group copy. It keeps account credentials, the stable device slot and ordinary chats, history, drafts and settings. It abandons old link-bound preparations; retained shared values and security decisions can synchronize again under ordinary rules. It sends no removal and repairs no ordinary-chat membership. It is separate from sign-out, account removal and a Move. An already unlinked device cannot use it to bypass removal.

Reset acts on this device, not the other slot named by a sign-in row. Check both devices before choosing which local copy to discard. If the approver still lists this slot, fresh admission can remain refused; removing that slot writes removal evidence and is not a universal shortcut back in. If no other device retains the old group, a later first link can create a different group: its discarded roster continuity is not restored. Independently retained local backup/security records are kept.

The returned link snapshot has no trusted old copy to restore. Reset does not publish a new KeyPackage. Use the normal rotate_key_package(account_ref) publication action, then start a fresh code-comparison flow and confirm on both devices; the fresh Welcome can join the same group id under the existing exact sender/group/KeyPackage checks. Reset alone does not guarantee admission: the approver may still list the slot or its old leaf, reject it, or be full. Existing duplicate, removal, capacity and authentication rules still apply. Cancellation or failure after reset can leave needs-link; a restart before confirmation can require a new exchange. A fresh link already confirmed retains its existing durable Welcome-wait/restart rules. Retained chat data guarantees neither current membership nor missing history backfill, and admitted work is not recalled.

Active pairing, an unfinished Move or unsettled native device-group work refuses with device_group_busy. Ordinary settlement may unblock it, but no deadline is promised. No trusted copy returns no_device_group; the command never creates a link or a new device slot. Rebuild matching native/generated bindings for the additive action and sign-in field. Actual app display adoption is separate.

Moving this device to another device group

In an experimental device-group build, start the same compared-code linking flow on a device that already trusts a device group to move only that device. Keep showing the existing group while DeviceLinkSnapshotFfi.moves is WaitingForWelcome or Joining. Joining the destination alone does not switch trust: Made requires this device's first selected authenticated change there. Its trust then switches once, with ordinary full small-state synchronization at unchanged versions. Chats and chat membership stay in place; the move does not promise delivery between the two device groups. Released binding builds still provide no working linking entry.

At most one confirmed move link is kept, with its Welcome expectation while that Welcome is pending. After restart another code comparison can begin, but if the earlier move is still pending at confirmation the new exchange ends before this device sends its Confirm (LinkFailed locally, CannotLink on the answering device). The earlier link and any still-live expectation stay unchanged; no second link approval or Add is made.

If this device moves while another device's link it approved is still pending, its old local prompt can end as failed and its automatic chat additions can be skipped even if the other device joined. Finish that link before moving when its completion and chat additions matter. Moving does not undo the other device's admitted membership.

Each move has an opaque move_id. old_siblings names recognized devices left in the old group; while question_suppressed is true, offer to link that device here rather than treating its sign-in as unknown. dismiss_device_group_move_sibling(account_ref, move_id, slot_id_hex) ends only that local recognition hint; it does not remove or link a device. A later confirmed link or selected departure ends the hint too. Slots in overridden_rejection_slots were already devices in the destination, so that destination entry took precedence over an old rejection. Moves carry rejected slots with their original ages, never rejected KeyPackages.

LinkedDeviceStatusFfi::Moved is the old group's own status for a moving device; its cleanup leaves the device's ordinary chats alone. Already admitted old-group traffic may finish through normal delivery rules before local old-group storage is forgotten; there is no immediate-quiet deadline or cancellation promise. Several old siblings can race cleanup, costing extra Commits and convergence passes under normal branch selection. A known failed link before Made forgets only the destination and keeps old trust. An unrecoverable destination keeps that trust while ordinary repair applies; it may stay pending indefinitely and need manual local recovery. While pending, this device cannot confirm another move or answer new pairing Requests. Corrupt or unreadable local move facts can fail progress/status reads and need manual local recovery or reset followed by a fresh compared-code link. Do not infer an unlinked state or expect an unlink notification for those errors, and never reconstruct old trust. Recognition hints suppress questions only on the mover. Old siblings can ask “Was this you?” after cleanup; the user can dismiss that prompt. An old in-flight chat Add can leave a membership leaf whose Welcome no longer reaches this device. Automatic gap filling may not replace that leaf; manual chat membership repair can be needed. Moving adds no duplicate-leaf cleanup or recall of admitted Adds.

This device unlinked

When another of the account's devices removes this one with remove_linked_device, the account stops on this device once it reads the removal, and nothing more is sent from it (mdk#2628):

  • MarmotEventFfi::DeviceUnlinked { account_id_hex, account_label } fires once, after the account is signed out. From then on the account's AccountSummaryFfi has unlinked and signed_out set, and both stay set.
  • Show that this device was unlinked from the account, and stop showing its local history.
  • Signing in to it, logging in to it or importing its key fails with MarmotKitError::AccountUnlinked. Offer sign_out_and_wipe, which skips leaving the account's chats and deleting its KeyPackage slot, since the other devices did both. Signing in again is then a new sign-in that links this device anew.

Signing out with linked devices

sign_out_and_wipe signs out through the account's other devices when this device has a linked device that is not signing out too (mdk#2628):

  • It first records in the device group that it is leaving and waits for that to settle, which can take about 30 seconds; show progress. It then leaves only the chats no other device can take it out of, deletes its KeyPackage slot and wipes. The other devices remove it from the device group and from the rest.
  • WipeOutcomeFfi.groups_left_to_siblings counts the chats it left to the other devices; groups_left counts those it left itself.
  • When it can't ask them in time, it tries to leave every chat itself, reporting any it can't in group_leave_failures, and sets siblings_not_reached. Tell the user their other devices couldn't be asked, and that those devices may still list this one until the user removes it from one of them.
  • The other devices list it with LinkedDeviceStatusFfi::Leaving until they remove it, then drop it.

Signing out is device-only and does not submit an account-wide Leave decision. An active admin cannot self-remove, so in a chat the account administers with another account, where none of its other devices has a leaf, signing out steps the account down first and then leaves (mdk#2818), with or without linked devices. One wait of about 30 seconds covers all such chats; show progress. Each counts in groups_left only once this device sees its removal; otherwise group_leave_failures says why: the step-down was not accepted in time, the account is off the admin list but its removal was not seen in time (it stays a member), or the account became the chat's last admin. A blocked leave ends that chat's wait. A chat this device was already leaving gets nothing new and joins the same wait. This device keeps its leaf, and the sign-out reports the chat, where the account is the last admin, where another of the account's devices stays in the chat, and once its device group removed it during the sign-out. An eligible sibling can still remove this device while the account remains an admin.

Sibling assistance requires a trusted device group with another Active or Inactive device and this device's own roster entry already carrying its tag signature key. Removal also needs a chat that supports same-account device removal and the required tagged leaves; groups_left_to_siblings is a handoff, not a completed-removal receipt. Outside admin chats, groups_left counts successful local leave calls, not confirmed membership removal. The call still attempts local account deletion after remote leave failures. Show the chats in group_leave_failures and check local_cleanup.completed independently; local cleanup completion does not establish that this device left every chat.

Overdue KeyPackage refresh

While this device trusts a device group, it announces each KeyPackage in its own roster entry before publishing it, so a device group that can't take that Commit holds the refresh back. key_package_refresh_overdue(account_ref) is true once the KeyPackage this device would publish is still unannounced and its slot's newest publication is a week old. Inviters stop treating the device as fresh at 30 days, so tell the user. A routine refresh never shows, and neither does one that is announced but failing at the relays. Re-read on MarmotEventFfi::KeyPackageRefreshOverdueChanged, which carries no device or group identities and, with device groups on, also fires once each time the account's worker opens or reconnects. It is false in ordinary opens without explicit experimental device-group intent.

Unrecognized sign-ins

unrecognized_sign_ins(account_ref) returns sign-ins of this account that this device does not recognize as UnrecognizedSignInFfi records, for a "Was this you?" prompt:

  • Each is a fresh, valid KeyPackage of the account in a slot that neither this device nor its device group's roster knows. The earliest to appear comes first.
  • before_this_device means this device's first check found it, so it was signed in before this device: ask whether the user still has it, with last_seen_at. For any other, ask whether it was them, with client and appeared_at. client is display only.
  • state is Prompt, NotNow, or LinkedElsewhere/RejectedElsewhere when another device answered while the prompt waited here. linked_by_slot_id_hex names the linking device for LinkedElsewhere.
  • previously_linked_here adds context only when this device retains a made approval for that slot in its current trusted group but its settled selected roster no longer lists it. Offer “A slot previously linked here is missing from this device's current device list. Open both devices to check the link.” It does not authenticate the current publication or prove permanent loss. Known local removal/rejection or matching retained departure evidence suppresses the context, conservatively including older departures of the same slot/key. Incomplete records, expired evidence, slot reuse and discovery also bound it. False means no affirmative local context, not “never linked.” Keep existing Not now/dismiss behavior; silence/decryption failure is not a reset signal. The user can explicitly choose local reset.
  • answer_sign_in(account_ref, slot_id_hex, response) takes NotNow, Reject or Dismiss. Reject drops the sign-in from this device's list and records its slot as rejected in the device group's roster; with no device group yet, it waits on this device. On another device, a new sign-in whose prompt still waits there turns RejectedElsewhere and stays until Dismiss; one put off with NotNow, or found before that device, leaves its list. Dismiss only ends a prompt another device answered. Linking one is device pairing's.
  • The account checks at open, every six hours, and soon after one of its KeyPackages arrives live. check_sign_ins(account_ref) checks now and returns the list after the check.
  • Re-read on MarmotEventFfi::UnrecognizedSignInsChanged, which carries no slots. With device groups on, it also fires once each time the account's worker opens or reconnects, so it may fire with no visible change.
  • The list is empty in ordinary opens without explicit experimental device-group intent.
  • start_fresh(account_ref) is "No, start fresh" when the user no longer has the devices the first check found: every sign-in from before this device is answered NotNow, now and when one is listed later. It rejects nothing and raises no compromise warning, so one of those devices can still link this one. It is refused before the first check (sign_ins_unchecked) and once this device trusts a device group (device_group_exists). started_fresh says whether the device did so and still has no device group: say that only chats it is invited to from now on are here. Re-read it after start_fresh and on LinkedDevicesChanged.

Compromise warning

compromise_warning(account_ref) returns the account's open compromise warning on this device as CompromiseWarningItemFfi records, the earliest gathered first. An empty list means no warning is open:

  • Each item means someone holding the account's signing key, or a session with its remote signer, published where the account's devices did not. RejectedSignIn is a sign-in answered This wasn't me, on this device or another; ForeignOwnSlotKeyPackage is a KeyPackage this device found in its own slot that it did not make, with its key_package_ref_hex. Only the device that found it warns of it, and it has replaced it. slot_id_hex and occurred_at say where and when.
  • Later releases add reasons. Show one the app does not know as a generic one.
  • The warning gathers this device's rejections and those in its device group's roster, so a rejection made on another device warns here too. Rejections already in the first roster this device trusts count as seen: the user saw them on the devices that were there. A rejected sign-in leaves the warning once its slot is linked as a device.
  • dismiss_compromise_warning(account_ref) marks everything the warning gathers as seen, on this device only. It stays closed until a new rejection arrives, and a rejection that branch selection drops and brings back stays seen.
  • The app writes the wording, and never says the account's devices stopped them.
  • Re-read on MarmotEventFfi::CompromiseWarningChanged, which carries no slots. With device groups on, it also fires once each time the account's worker opens, so it may fire with no visible change.
  • The list is empty in ordinary opens without explicit experimental device-group intent.

Linking a new device

Linking a new device of the account shows the same seven emoji on both devices, and each user confirms. Every call returns a DeviceLinkSnapshotFfi, and every call requires the explicit experimental build and constructor described above:

  • The new device calls start_device_link(account_ref) and shows new_device: WaitingForAnswer (ask the user to open the app on a device already signed in), then Comparing with the code. Offer "They match" (confirm_device_link_match) and cancel (cancel_device_link). It then shows WaitingForOtherDevice, Joining, and Linked, or Ended with a reason.
  • A device already signed in shows each entry in prompts. Comparing shows the code; offer a label field, "Add to all my chats" and "Bring chat history" (both on by default), Link device (link_device) and Not now (decline_device_link). After Link device it shows Linking until the new device's first change in the device group arrives, then Linked; with none within an hour, the device is removed again and both sides show LinkFailed. Other states say why Link isn't offered, or AddedElsewhere: "<device_label> was added by <added_by_label>".
  • Each emoji carries an English description for screen readers. Users compare the pictures, not the descriptions.
  • device_link_snapshot(account_ref) reads linking without changing it. Re-read on MarmotEventFfi::DeviceLinkChanged, which carries no device, session or group identities. With device groups on, it also fires once each time the account's worker opens or reconnects. Live comparison sessions are lost then; admitted moves resume from durable progress. Inspect moves rather than assuming an interrupted comparison undid an admitted move.

Backup recovery and background conditions

Backup setup and manual restore require a dev-device-groups build opened with newWithExperimentalDeviceGroups (see experimental device-group test builds); both are off by default. Otherwise every backup call is refused with roster_unsupported, and ordinary hosts have nothing to do. MDK owns backup selection, due work, download limits, import validation and membership checks; the host supplies platform facts, renders status and obtains recovery words from the user.

Use beginRecoveryWords(accountRef) to generate 12 new words for backup setup. Display them once, then ask for the words at the two returned 1-based confirmPositions, in order, and pass those answers to confirmRecoveryWords. cancelRecoveryWords forgets the pending setup; backupSettings reads selected account settings. turnOffBackups disables future account backups without deleting existing archives. A busy or failed confirmation keeps the core setup available for another try. Read settings again rather than treating a submitted choice as settled.

Report setRuntimeBackupBackgroundConditions(wifi, charging) once per runtime, before workers exist and on changes. Background writer work requires both Wi-Fi and charging. Reports survive account-worker restarts; a new runtime starts closed. An admitted pass settles after false, while later passes wait. The account-shaped setBackupBackgroundConditions remains a compatibility wrapper that validates the active account before reporting the same runtime-wide facts and never starts its worker. Manual restore is independent.

An OS background task can await runDueBackupPass(accountRef): it joins the current pass or tries ordinary due admission once. The admission wait includes other queued work and startup catch-up. NotStarted admits nothing; FinishedAttempt means the pass's serialized settlement attempt and credit release ended. It is not a publication-success receipt, forced backup, future-due wait or whole-runtime idle barrier. Cancelling this caller detaches its wait; worker stop/replacement returns TransportClosed. The host bounds its OS execution opportunity, since a queued caller's wait has no additional timeout, and supplies fresh facts to each new runtime. Disabled device-group support returns NotStarted without starting a worker; the fact-report method itself is local and available.

beginBackupRestore(accountRef, words) starts one manual history-only operation per account and returns its status. Old words remain usable independently of the current backup key; restore never enables backups or changes that key. Only chats whose current selected MLS tree contains this device's own leaf can receive history. Unknown chats retain private availability metadata, without creating or joining a chat. After a real join, backupHistoryAvailability returns words-again hints for that current chat. Archived preferences and invitation decisions are not applied.

Use backupRestoreStatus or watchBackupRestore for aggregate progress. A watch offers its initial snapshot once and then next updates; closing it does not cancel work. Complete means eligible work settled, not that all history was found or that a backup pointer existed. Partial retains committed history; Unavailable can require a later manual retry. Availability revisions wake the same watch; read the current chat's hints again. Operation tokens are opaque, ephemeral, account-scoped strings: return the exact token to cancelBackupRestore. A stale valid token returns false and cannot cancel a newer operation; malformed tokens are rejected. Cancellation and shutdown release owned secrets and leave committed history intact. Retry explicitly with the words again; there is no durable secret-backed resume.

Timeline pages and prepared conversation rows expose historyImportProvenance: Device carries a device slot, Backup carries an archive identity. Render backup rows as restored from backup, never as an unnamed device. The archive identity does not prove original writer, historical authorship or historical membership. The legacy importedFrom field remains sibling-only; its absence alone does not identify live rows.

Never persist, log or include recovery words in diagnostics. Clear host-owned input and displayed copies promptly. MDK guards its owned queued phrases and confirmation answers and zeroizes managed secret buffers on release; generated Swift/Kotlin strings, caller copies and upstream parser/hash/compiler scratch are outside that guarantee. Dropping a managed string does not promise erasure. Do not log whole DTOs even when a particular Rust Debug implementation redacts them.

History may be incomplete notices

Automatic recovery stops retrying an obligation after a fixed budget of attempts that recover and certify nothing. Each such parked occurrence is a notice the user should see as "history may be incomplete":

  • history_notices(account_ref) returns HistoryNoticeFfi records, oldest first: an opaque notice_id, a HistoryNoticeCauseFfi for the host's wording, group_id_hex for a group-scoped occurrence (an epoch gap) or None when the account as a whole is affected (delivery or notification loss, incremental or explicit history), and an optional parked_at_ms. It reads local durable state and never touches the network.
  • group_recovery_status sets history_may_be_incomplete and lists the group's own history_notice_ids. Show a banner in that conversation; account-wide notices belong in an account-level surface instead.
  • MarmotEventFfi::HistoryNoticesChanged fires when a notice appears (recovery parked), disappears (new evidence re-armed recovery, or it was dismissed), or is replaced. Re-read the list; a group whose own notices changed also receives GroupStateUpdated.
  • dismiss_history_notice(account_ref, notice_id) records the user's decision durably, as its own outcome and never as recovered history. It returns false for a stale id; re-read and show the current notices. After a delivery-loss dismissal the transport cursor can advance again once no loss recovery remains pending.

Do not dismiss on the user's behalf, and do not persist notice_id as a group or account identity: it changes whenever recovery re-arms. A dismissed occurrence never comes back, but genuinely new evidence can raise a new notice: new loss, a higher missing epoch, a later startup's incremental comparison, or a new explicit repair. Explicit full-history repair remains available and can still complete parked history that its comparison of the retained window certifies. Notices carry no relay, message or key identities; keep them out of analytics. C callers: see the C guide.

account_recovery_status(account_ref) returns AccountRecoveryStatusFfi: the groups whose history is still being fetched (catching_up_group_ids_hex), whether the inbox's is (inbox_catching_up), and every notice as history_notices lists them. Show the first two as "catching up" and re-read on MarmotEventFfi::RecoveryStatusChanged. The recovery runner supplies those fields. Current epoch-gap exhaustion emits EpochGap; coverage-ledger parks emit HistoryNoticeCauseFfi::UnprovenHistory without attributing the original reason history was owed. Other cause labels preserve compatibility; keep exhaustive switches.

When a Welcome installs a new copy of a group in place of this device's old one (an automatic rejoin after the old copy could not be repaired, a reentry after a trusted removal, or a fork discarded with the user's consent, whose old copy may still have worked), the group gets one HistoryNoticeCauseFfi::BeforeRejoin notice: messages from before the rejoin that the device had not received are unavailable, and recovery stopped fetching them. A restart raises no second one, dismissing it retires nothing further, and a later rejoin raises a new one.

Durably and natively Unrecoverable copies start authenticated automatic rejoin in the existing account workers. Hosts use the existing Repair action to rearm an eligible parked episode; restarting alone does not reset its budget. A reachable eligible admin and eventual delivery are required. Usable forks still need explicit replacement consent, and pruned epoch secrets are not restored. See the automatic rejoin contract.

While unresolved epoch-gap recovery covers a group's current local epoch, the group may have moved past this device. Group changes (invite, remove, admin changes, profile, image, retention, disbanding and app components) then fail with MarmotKitError::GroupCatchingUp: a change committed from a stale epoch can split the group for everyone. Messages and leaving are not affected.

The check is advisory, because the evidence behind it cannot be authenticated. Ask the user, for example: "This chat may be out of date on this device. Changing the group now could split it for everyone. Wait for it to sync, or continue anyway?" To continue, call acknowledge_group_catching_up(account_ref, group_id_hex) and retry the change. The acknowledgement admits one change attempt at the device's current epoch, is consumed even if that attempt fails, and is not persisted. Use the strongest wording for invites: a member invited onto a branch that later loses is left with a Welcome that no longer works. Without an acknowledgement, the check lifts once recovery catches the group up or the device moves past that epoch. Dismissing the group's history notice does not lift it. Scheduled self-updates wait up to a day for the group to catch up, then proceed.

A group change counts as published once one group relay accepts it, and MDK keeps retrying the other group relays with the same event. Until they accept it, members who read only those relays cannot follow the group. Once a change has been owed to a relay for two minutes (a healthy slower relay is retried after 30 seconds), group changes fail with MarmotKitError::GroupCommitUndelivered (mdk#2255). group_commit_delivery(account_ref, group_id_hex) returns the oldest change still owed to a relay, with the relays owing it and since (when the first relay accepted it), or None. It is reported immediately, so a host can show "not delivered to every relay yet" before the user tries a change; a Some result alone does not mean the next change fails. No event announces delivery completing, so poll while showing it. This check is advisory too, because groups often list a relay that is gone for good: once the user accepts that members on those relays may not follow, call acknowledge_group_commit_undelivered(account_ref, group_id_hex) and retry. Like the catching-up acknowledgement, it admits one change attempt and is not persisted. A change can need both acknowledgements; each survives the other check refusing the attempt. Scheduled self-updates wait up to an hour for delivery, then proceed.

File-backed media upload

Use uploadMediaFiles for private regular-file inputs instead of sending a whole-file byte array across the binding. uploadMediaFilesWithClientToken preserves durable local-send admission; probe localSendStatus after an unknown outcome before another upload. Keep the host source valid until return, use one MediaFileTransferControlFfi per operation, and explicitly cancel it rather than only dropping the host's wait. Every source is copied into the account's encrypted media store before PUT, and the ciphertext streams from that copy without being written to disk. A source the disk cannot hold beyond the attachment policy's disk reserve fails with StorageFull before anything is uploaded; ask the user to free space. The counter is monotonic processed bytes (copy, digest pass, then transfer), not a percentage.

Uploads return MediaAttachmentReferenceFfi.sourceEpochIdentity, a local branch identity that must be preserved unchanged when saving a reference or passing it to sendMediaAttachments, sendTaggedMedia, or reactWithMedia. A send requires both the upload epoch and that exact branch to remain current. A branch change can invalidate an upload even when the epoch number stays the same. References received from peers or saved before this field existed have no upload identity: re-upload their retained bytes before sending them. Downloads of those references remain supported. This identity is local metadata and is never included in imeta or shared with peers.

Cancellation observed before message admission starts prevents publication. Admission is not interruptible once started, including while durable acceptance is pending. File-backed uploads have no fixed worker-response timeout; per-endpoint network deadlines still apply.

maxFileMediaCiphertextBytes includes a 16-byte AEAD tag for each attachment in the batch. This is a finite implementation bound, not a claimed server maximum. Uploads try policy endpoints in order; ordinary rejection or invalid descriptors fall through, while signer denial and cancellation stop the operation. An explicit endpoint override intentionally selects only that endpoint. Receiver acquisition streams large bodies into private files, resumes protected ciphertext where valid, and authenticates before publishing bounded readable local assets. The stored copy becomes the sender's local attachment once the message is confirmed, with no retention budget. Preview limits and the legacy byte-array API bounds are not increased.

See the upload reference and local-send ownership. C hosts use the file-backed C inputs and control.

Bounded attachment history

Use the asynchronous attachment history page/version methods for canonical media-library discovery. See the native handoff for filtering, refresh, removal and cursor ownership. list_media remains a compatibility API. Custom reaction artwork uses the bounded reactionAttachment lookup with the reaction event ID, followed by the same acquisition and local-read path as chat attachments; see reaction artwork.

Local attachment access

Use attachmentLocalAssets to locate verified retained bytes for visible source slots, then readAttachmentAsset for bounded local chunks without network work. See the native attachment handoff for unavailable/EOF semantics, source revalidation, host buffer ownership and integration guidance. For an OS surface that needs a real file (package installer, share sheet, "open with", Quick Look), use openAttachmentHandoff and release its lease when done; see handoff leases. A Manage storage screen reads usage and largest-first listings, removes attachments in bulk and sets the opt-in "Keep media" window; see Manage storage. Acquisition defaults on with bounded per-account policy. Native progress snapshots/subscriptions and durable cancellation, retry, remove and download-again controls use the same source slots.

Audit v5 recording and delivery

v5 replaces v4 as the audit format. AuditLogSettingsFfi.enabled remains the recording opt-in. Account sessions and the live runtime write only marmot-forensics-audit/v5 to audit-<engine_id>-v5.jsonl; no new v4 files are written, and existing v4 files remain on disk. Hosts that record audit logs must configure v5 delivery, or new evidence never leaves the device. Deploy a receiver that accepts every v5 event kind first.

To deliver v5, supply a dedicated OTLP /v1/logs destination and bearer token with set_audit_otlp_config_v5(AuditOtlpConfigV5Ffi). The configuration is held in memory, so apply it on every launch; the returned record omits the token. Set enabled: false to remove delivery configuration. An exact loopback endpoint requires allow_loopback_dev: true; public endpoints require HTTPS. The host then calls post_audit_log_tracker_update_v5(), in place of post_audit_log_tracker_update(), for an immediate pass; the existing audit tracker also uses this configuration on its activity triggers with the usual batching, retry, and shutdown behavior. The v5 result reports accepted batches, pending accounts, blocked accounts, and idle accounts separately from legacy v4 uploads. No host should infer receiver acceptance from an empty v4 uploaded list. The v4 whole-file Goggles endpoint never receives v5 records.

Legacy audit v4 upload

The v4 whole-file route only drains v4 files written before 0.11.0; keep its configuration until they are gone, and do not build new v4 infrastructure. Whole-file uploads accept only marmot-forensics-audit/v4; older local files are never migrated or sent. App construction automatically removes recognized v1-v3 forensic files and rotated segments after acquiring the root lease, including files in failed account-wipe remnants, even with recording disabled. V4 files and the separate key-reveal log are preserved; failures are nonfatal and retried on the next open. No additional Swift/Kotlin cleanup call is needed.

Use AuditLogTrackerConfigV4Ffi with AuditLogUploadSourceV4Ffi.hardwareModel in place of the old source record and its deviceLabel. The versioned config type changes the setter ABI checksum so old generated bindings cannot silently reinterpret a device label as a hardware model. Populate this field from system model information (e.g. iPhone17,3 or Pixel 9a), never from a device name, hostname or serial number. Omit it if unavailable. Platform and app version are unchanged. Uploads of leftover v4 files still need a v4-compatible Goggles endpoint; new evidence goes to v5.

Native metadata lift/lower checks: ./crates/marmot-uniffi/audit-v4-smoke.sh swift and MDK_KOTLIN_CLASSPATH=<JNA:Android:annotations:coroutines jars> ./crates/marmot-uniffi/audit-v4-smoke.sh kotlin. These regenerate host bindings and execute DTO round trips; platform package builds remain separate.

Building local bindings

The Rust API in src/ is the source of truth for both generated Swift and generated Kotlin. Platform scripts only package that shared surface:

  • ./crates/marmot-uniffi/xcframework.sh builds output/MarmotKit.xcframework plus output/MarmotKit.swift and output/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy for iOS.
  • ./crates/marmot-uniffi/xcframework-macos.sh builds output/macos/MarmotKit.xcframework plus output/macos/MarmotKit.swift and output/macos/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy for macOS on Apple Silicon (aarch64-apple-darwin). Its output directory is separate from the iOS one so building both in one workspace cannot clobber either artifact.
  • ./crates/marmot-uniffi/kotlin-bindings.sh builds output/android/kotlin/dev/ipf/marmotkit/marmot_uniffi.kt plus Android jniLibs shared libraries.

Building from source also requires Odin dev-2026-10 at the pinned revision, because Markdown parsing is compiled from Odin. Install it with bash scripts/install-odin.sh <dir> and set ODIN to the compiler, as the workspace README shows. Published artifacts already contain the compiled parser.

The generated Swift file is platform-independent: output/MarmotKit.swift and output/macos/MarmotKit.swift are the same UniFFI surface, and releases publish it once. The Kotlin binding is generated from the same host library metadata, so it exposes the same Marmot object, subscription objects, records, enums, and error variants.

No generated Swift or Kotlin files are committed here; the output directories are ignored because generated bindings and packaged native libraries are derived artifacts. Regenerate them from this crate before vendoring into an app repository. For published artifacts, exact release and snapshot URLs, checksums, provenance and generated-source synchronization rules, see DISTRIBUTION.md.

Build phases

The no-argument build scripts still build complete local bundles. Release CI uses separate phases to parallelize compilation across runners:

Script Phase Work
xcframework.sh generate Host library and generated Swift/headers in build/ios/swift; no device builds
xcframework.sh native <target> One aarch64-apple-ios or aarch64-apple-ios-sim native build
xcframework.sh assemble Assemble existing native slices and build/ios/swift into the usual iOS output
xcframework-macos.sh native One aarch64-apple-darwin build with the macOS deployment flags
xcframework-macos.sh assemble Assemble the native slice with shared Swift/headers placed in build/macos/swift
kotlin-bindings.sh generate Host library, generated Kotlin and Android support files; no NDK required
kotlin-bindings.sh native JNI libraries for ANDROID_ABIS; no host library or binding generation

Run independent phases in separate checkouts/runners. Multiple Cargo processes sharing one target directory contend on its lock; separate phases do not make concurrent invocations in one checkout safe. All inputs must have matching source, builder, toolchain, profile and features. CI transfers inputs only within the same workflow run. Apple assembly checks required files before replacing an existing bundle and never compiles Rust. Both Apple scripts honor CARGO_TARGET_DIR. See the release guide for the build-only benchmark workflow.

Kotlin / Android

Prerequisites:

rustup target add aarch64-linux-android armv7-linux-androideabi i686-linux-android x86_64-linux-android
# macOS Android Studio default:
export ANDROID_NDK_HOME="$HOME/Library/Android/sdk/ndk/<version>"
# Linux / common CI default:
# export ANDROID_NDK_HOME="$HOME/Android/Sdk/ndk/<version>"

CI jobs can also set ANDROID_SDK_ROOT or ANDROID_HOME; the build script will discover the newest NDK under $ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/ndk or $ANDROID_HOME/ndk when ANDROID_NDK_HOME is not set.

Build all Android ABIs, or a subset:

./crates/marmot-uniffi/kotlin-bindings.sh
ANDROID_ABIS="arm64-v8a x86_64" ./crates/marmot-uniffi/kotlin-bindings.sh

Generated Kotlin uses package dev.ipf.marmotkit, loads libmarmot_uniffi.so, and requires the normal UniFFI Kotlin runtime dependencies used by the generated file: JNA, Kotlin coroutines, and AndroidX annotations.

The script keeps the host library's UniFFI metadata intact while stripping debug and static symbol sections from each packaged Android JNI library. The two 64-bit ABIs (arm64-v8a, x86_64) are linked with 16 KB ELF PT_LOAD alignment for Google Play's 16 KB page-size check; the 32-bit ABIs stay on the NDK's default page size. Aligning the app bundle ZIP does not change those segments. Each published Android archive includes an android-elf.json report of the packaged libraries' hashes and observed load alignments; see DISTRIBUTION.md. That report does not by itself prove an app's Play Console result.

Android initialization (required before the first Marmot(...))

Marmot(...) constructs the Android-native keyring store, which talks to the Android Keystore over JNI and needs the ndk-context initialized with the application Context first. The build copies two hand-written helpers (kotlin-support/) next to the generated binding:

  • dev.ipf.marmotkit.MarmotAndroid — the call consumers use.
  • io.crates.keyring.Keyring — the JNI shim the android-native-keyring-store crate requires (statically linked into libmarmot_uniffi.so, so its symbol is exported from that library).

Android consumers MUST call MarmotAndroid.initialize(this) from Application.onCreate before constructing Marmot, otherwise the first constructor crashes with android context was not initialized:

class MarmotApplication : Application() {
    override fun onCreate() {
        super.onCreate()
        MarmotAndroid.initialize(this)
    }
}

iOS does not need this — apple-native-keyring-store uses Keychain APIs that do not require a JavaVM. If the host framework already initialized ndk-context, do not call initialize again.

Release profile

Standard MarmotKit release builds use the workspace [profile.release] together with marmotkit-release-profile.env: lto=thin, codegen-units=1, opt-level=3, debug=0, panic=unwind, and strip=none. Android target invocations override only CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP=symbols. Apple target invocations add -C embed-bitcode=no and sanitize leftover __LLVM / __bitcode sections before packaging so shipped archives stay native; that is not a symbol strip. Sanitization requires the active Rust toolchain's llvm-tools-preview component (included by rust-toolchain.toml) and Xcode's libtool. It rebuilds symbol indexes and validates a temporary output before replacing the original archive. Those builder-owned settings are not a user-facing escape hatch; measurement scripts may override LTO and codegen units on direct Cargo commands for a controlled baseline comparison.

These are configured profile values, not proof that Cargo applies LTO to every output: the mixed rlib/cdylib/staticlib binding target can suppress LTO. The measured reduction belongs to the combined profile, not to thin LTO alone. Apple measurement rows record pre-sanitization Cargo archive bytes and hashes, not final packaged-archive or linked application sizes. Native-only archive validation and consumer linking are separate packaging checks. Changing crate types to enable effective LTO also requires revisiting the incompatible embed-bitcode=no flag and revalidating native Apple artifacts. The latest recorded comparison is in release-profile-measurements.md.

The automatic MarmotKit Release Profile workflow (bindings-profile.yml) is an exact-head packaging check, not a comparison benchmark. It builds Kotlin/Swift generation and every Android or Apple native target once in parallel, transfers those inputs only within the current workflow run, verifies their source, builder, toolchain, profile, feature and run provenance, then assembles and validates the Android, iOS and macOS candidate packages. Full packaging is opt-in on pull requests: ci:android selects Kotlin generation and all four Android ABIs, ci:apple selects the Apple inputs and packages, and ci:full selects both platforms. After adding a packaging label, re-run all candidate-workflow jobs or push a new commit; the workflow reads the current labels. Ordinary PRs retain Rust compilation/API and packaging-contract checks without building complete candidate bundles. Android target compilation, NDK checks and native linking are deferred unless explicitly selected, including for changes to the UniFFI crate. Matching master pushes always build the complete matrix and open an issue when it fails; later pushes do not cancel running or queued candidate builds. Candidate builds use no Cargo cache, so every run compiles from a clean target directory. The workflow has no schedule of its own. The nightly release builds and validates the same Android and Apple packages from master, but only on nights it does not skip: it skips when master has no new green commit or is not on an X.Y.Z-dev version, and when releases or snapshots keep the macOS runners busy for three hours. It does not run test-native-archive.py; matching master pushes do.

Baseline-versus-candidate measurements are intentionally manual. Run the MarmotKit Release Profile Measurements workflow from master with the full lowercase SHA that needs fresh evidence (it must already be fetchable from GitHub):

gh workflow run bindings-profile-measurement.yml \
  --ref master \
  -f source_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"

The non-publishing run fails closed unless checkout matches the SHA exactly, and uploads separate Linux/Android/CPU and Apple reports, hashes, raw Criterion output and build logs. A failed or incomplete surface keeps the final comparison check red. Local equivalents:

# Inexpensive regressions, including provenance JSON and archive bitcode checks:
python3 crates/marmot-uniffi/test-release-profile.py

# On macOS: real archive reconstruction, embedded-bitcode removal and linking:
python3 crates/marmot-uniffi/test-native-archive.py

# Controlled host/Android/Apple/CPU comparison. Missing platforms are recorded as
# unavailable, never as zero. Isolated target directories keep the two variants
# from overwriting each other. `--cpu` fails if a benchmark invocation fails or
# only stale Criterion estimates remain:
python3 crates/marmot-uniffi/measure-release-profile.py \
  --source-sha "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" \
  --builder-sha "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" \
  --host --cpu \
  --output release-profile-measurements.json \
  --markdown release-profile-measurements.md

Apple privacy resources

Apple exporters use raw static-library slices and publish a matching privacy manifest for the consuming Swift target. See the privacy audit and adoption guide for declarations, archive validation, host integration changes, and unresolved release questions.

Account attachment history

account_attachment_history_page reads bounded indexed attachment candidates across one local account. Original album slots retain source identity and shared-parser metadata; group/sender selections and inclusive dates bind the cursor. Empty filtered pages may still continue, and destructive source changes require replacing loaded rows; additions offer a separate head refresh. Reads perform no acquisition or decryption. See Account attachment history for integration and bounds.
